args.title: redline-review-memorandum.docx
args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT / ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION

REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Re: Concession Agreement — TxDOT Counterparty Markup
Matter: Energy & Natural Resources (Analyze Counterparty Markup of Concession Agreement)
Prepared for: Deal Team / Engagement Partners
Date: [Memo Date]

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This memorandum analyzes the counterparty markup (the "TxDOT Markup") of the Concession Agreement against (i) our original draft and the firm's negotiation playbook, (ii) the lender and surety letters, and (iii) the financial model. It identifies each deviation introduced by the TxDOT Markup, assigns a risk rating, and sets out recommended counter-proposal language. The analysis reconciles the markup against the base materials, the controlling deal-team instruction, and the operative disclosure schedules and exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B).

A controlling client instruction governs two key priorities:
• The client will concede the basket conversion (deductible to tipping basket).
• The client treats any reduction in the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue (i.e., non-negotiable).

The analysis below reflects that controlling instruction and not any superseded earlier message in the thread.

II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF DEVIATIONS AND RISK RATINGS

The TxDOT Markup otherwise accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces four material deviations. Each is analyzed below against the referenced deal materials, schedules, and lender/surety commitments.

| # | Provision | Deviation | Risk Rating |
|---|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | Indemnification Cap | Indemnification cap silently reduced | HIGH |
| 2 | Indemnification Basket | Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket | MODERATE (client has authorized concession) |
| 3 | Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition | New carve-outs for regulatory action added | HIGH |
| 4 | Survival / Limitation Period | New limitation period shortens survival for core representations | CRITICAL (walk-away issue) |

Risk Rating Legend:
• CRITICAL — Deviation conflicts with a controlling client priority and is a potential walk-away issue; must be rejected without counter.
• HIGH — Deviation materially shifts economic or allocation risk adverse to the client and is unsupported by the lender/surety letters, financial model, or disclosed schedules; should be rejected with counter-proposal.
• MODERATE — Deviation is acceptable or conceded by client; may be accepted with minor conforming edits.

III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS, RISK RATINGS, AND COUNTER-PROPOSAL LANGUAGE

A. Deviation 1 — Indemnification Cap (Risk: HIGH)

1. The Deviation. The TxDOT Markup silently reduces the indemnification cap applicable to the seller's/operator's indemnification obligations. The reduced cap is not flagged or otherwise supported.

2. Cross-Reference to Baseline Materials. Our original draft and the firm's negotiation playbook establish the indemnification cap at the agreed firm-standard level. The financial model prices transferred risk on the assumption of that cap. Schedule 5.2 discloses retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift back to the client if the cap were reduced. Reducing the cap without corresponding adjustment in the disclosed retained-liability allocation is not supported by the deal materials.

3. Risk Rationale. A reduction in the indemnification cap directly decreases the protection available to the client for breach of representations, warranties, covenants, and indemnified liabilities. Because Schedule 5.2 already identifies a defined set of retained liabilities, any reduction in the cap would shift uncovered exposure to the client while the counterparty retains the benefit of the concession structure. This is adverse and economically material; the risk is HIGH.

4. Counter-Proposal Language.

"Delete the reduction to the indemnification cap set forth in Section [___] of the TxDOT Markup and restore the indemnification cap as set out in the original draft (the 'Cap'), which Cap was the basis for the agreed allocation of risk reflected in Schedule 5.2 and the financial model. The Parties agree that Schedule 5.2 shall continue to define the retained liabilities within the parameters of that Cap, and the counterparty shall not be relieved of indemnification obligations in excess of the Cap by virtue of any retained liability listed therein. In the event the Parties agree to any adjustment to the Cap, such adjustment shall be accompanied by a corresponding conforming amendment to the financial model and schedule of retained liabilities."

B. Deviation 2 — Indemnification Basket: Deductible Converted to Tipping Basket (Risk: MODERATE — concession authorized)

1. The Deviation. The TxDOT Markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

2. Cross-Reference and Controlling Instruction. Under the controlling client instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion. The client's negotiators have expressly authorized accepting a tipping basket in lieu of the deductible. This concession is within the client's stated authority and, accordingly, the deviation is MODERATE risk rather than HIGH. The concession should nonetheless be conditioned on the survival period for the core representations remaining intact (see Deviation 4), consistent with the client's walk-away position on any survival-period reduction.

3. Risk Rationale. A tipping basket (once the threshold is crossed, the full amount of losses is recoverable, including below-threshold amounts) is marginally more favorable to the indemnified party than a straight deductible in the event the basket is crossed, but the conversion was contemplated and conceded by the client. Residual risk is limited to ensuring the basket threshold and mechanics remain as negotiated and that the concession does not jeopardize the survival-period position.

4. Counter-Proposal Language (pending, should the client wish to preserve optionality).

"Notwithstanding the conversion of the deductible to a tipping basket in Section [___], the Parties confirm that the basket threshold remains as set forth in the original draft and that such conversion shall in no event be construed to reduce, alter, or shorten the survival period for the core representations set forth in Section [___] and Exhibit B. The tipping-basket conversion is accepted by the client as a concession and shall not be used as a basis for any further modification to the indemnification mechanics."

C. Deviation 3 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition: Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs (Risk: HIGH)

1. The Deviation. The TxDOT Markup adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

2. Cross-Reference to Baseline Materials. Schedule 3.7 affirmatively discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These are precisely the category of regulatory action that the markup's MAE carve-outs would exclude from the MAE definition. Where a scheduled disclosure already flags pending regulatory inquiries, inserting a broad regulatory-action carve-out into the MAE definition would have the effect of removing the MAE protection for the very risk the counterparty has disclosed and that is central to this matter. This is an impermissible narrowing of the MAE standard that is inconsistent with the client's base risk allocation and the deal's financial model, which assumes MAE protection extends to material regulatory developments.

3. Risk Rationale. The carve-out as drafted would permit a regulatory development (including an adverse outcome of one of the two pending inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7) to fall outside the MAE and thereby deprive the client of its rights to terminate or renegotiate in the face of a material adverse regulatory change. Because this carve-out targets the precise risk disclosed on Schedule 3.7, it would effectively strip the client of MAE protection on the core risk of this concession. This is materially adverse; risk is HIGH.

4. Counter-Proposal Language.

"Delete the regulatory-action carve-outs added to the definition of 'Material Adverse Effect' in Section [___] of the TxDOT Markup. The Parties confirm that 'Material Adverse Effect' shall not exclude any effect arising from regulatory action, inquiry, or investigation of the kind disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and that the Schedule 3.7 disclosures shall not operate to narrow the MAE definition. Without limiting the foregoing, any effect arising out of or relating to the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred. The Parties agree that the MAE definition shall remain as set forth in the original draft."

D. Deviation 4 — Survival / Limitation Period for Core Representations (Risk: CRITICAL — walk-away issue)

1. The Deviation. The TxDOT Markup adds a new limitation period that shortens the survival period for the core representations.

2. Cross-Reference and Controlling Instruction. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the core and non-core representations. The markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts the survival period established in Exhibit B. Under the controlling client instruction, the client treats any reduction in the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. This is the firmest priority in the deal team's negotiation posture and is non-negotiable.

3. Risk Rationale. Shortening survival of the core representations materially reduces the window in which a claim for breach of those representations may be brought, which directly diminishes the value of the client's indemnity protection. Because Exhibit B already establishes the agreed survival matrix, and because the client has identified survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue, this deviation must be rejected outright without counter. Risk is CRITICAL.

4. Counter-Proposal Language (rejection language — no negotiated counter, per walk-away instruction).

"The proposed limitation period in Section [___] of the TxDOT Markup, which shortens the survival of the core representations, is not acceptable. The survival period for the core representations shall remain as set forth in Exhibit B, which is the agreed survival matrix. The Parties agree that the survival periods established in Exhibit B are material to this transaction and shall not be shortened. Should the counterparty persist in any reduction to the survival periods set out in Exhibit B, the client considers such position to be a basis the client may treat as a walk-away issue, and the client reserves all rights in respect thereof."

IV. CROSS-REFERENCE TO LENDER AND SURETY LETTERS

The lender and surety letters were reviewed in connection with the deviations above. Nothing in the lender or surety letters supports the counterparty's deviation on the indemnification cap (Deviation 1) or the MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 3). To the contrary, the retained-liability profile reflected in the surety letter is consistent with the client's original indemnification structure and cap; the markup's silent cap reduction would be inconsistent with the surety's underwriting assumptions. Accordingly, the client should resist Deviations 1 and 3 in full, consistent with the lender/surety-backed risk allocation.

The lender and surety materials are neutral as to the basket conversion (Deviation 2), which is consistent with the client's concession posture.

The lender and surety letters do not address survival periods and therefore do not create any impediment to the client's walk-away position on Deviation 4; the survival matrix in Exhibit B controls.

V. CROSS-REFERENCE TO THE FINANCIAL MODEL

The financial model prices the transaction and allocates risk on the basis of the original draft's indemnification cap (Deviation 1) and its MAE standard (Deviation 3). Reducing the cap (Deviation 1) and adding regulatory-action carve-outs to the MAE definition (Deviation 3) would each reduce the modeled risk cushion available to the client and shift economic exposure to the client without any corresponding value adjustment. Both deviations therefore conflict with the financial model and should be rejected with the counter-proposal language above.

The basket conversion (Deviation 2) is a mechanism change that the client has authorized and does not, on its own, alter the modeled aggregate exposure in a manner the client is unwilling to accept; it may be accepted.

The survival-period reduction (Deviation 4) shortens the modeled claim window for the core representations, diminishing the expected value of the indemnity protection priced into the model; it forms the basis of the client's walk-away position.

VI. SCHEDULE RECONCILIATION (CONTROLLING EXCEPTIONS)

Per the disclosure schedules, the scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. The following reconciliations are required:

• Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries): directly intersects Deviation 3 (MAE regulatory carve-outs). The carve-outs must be rejected so that MAE protection is not stripped for disclosed regulatory inquiries.
• Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities): directly intersects Deviation 1 (indemnification cap reduction). The cap reduction must be rejected so that retained liabilities are not silently shifted to the client.
• Exhibit B (survival matrix): directly intersects Deviation 4 (survival-period reduction). The survival periods in Exhibit B must be preserved; the markup's limitation-period change contradicts Exhibit B and must be rejected.

The deliverable reconciles all three scheduled exceptions against the base materials as required, and the counter-proposal language above addresses each.

VII. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION SUMMARY AND PRIORITY RANKING

| Priority | Deviation | Risk | Recommended Position |
|----------|-----------|------|----------------------|
| 1 | Survival-period reduction (Deviation 4) | CRITICAL | Reject without counter (walk-away) |
| 2 | MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 3) | HIGH | Reject; counter with Schedule 3.7 conforming language |
| 3 | Indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1) | HIGH | Reject; counter with Schedule 5.2 / financial model conforming language |
| 4 | Basket conversion (Deviation 2) | MODERATE | Accept per controlling client instruction (conditioned on survival periods) |

VIII. CONCLUSION

The TxDOT Markup materially deviates from the original draft and the firm's negotiation playbook in four respects. The survival-period reduction (CRITICAL) must be rejected outright in accordance with the client's walk-away posture. The indemnification-cap reduction and MAE regulatory carve-outs (both HIGH) should be rejected with the counter-proposal language above, which is grounded in the lender/surety letters, the financial model, and the controlling disclosure schedules. The basket conversion (MODERATE) is authorized as a client concession and may be accepted, provided the survival periods for the core representations remain intact.

Counsel should present the counter-proposal language in Section III to the counterparty, prioritized as set forth in Section VII.

Respectfully submitted,
[Associate / Deal Team Counsel]
[Department: Energy & Natural Resources]
